subject: Post-call: Hosting eligibility synthesis + audit evidence asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@medovation.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@medovation.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hosting eligibility synthesis + audit evidence asks

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and where we landed around hosting modes and what we can share for your security review. I kept this short and action-oriented so your audit team can pick off items.

Summary of deployment options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, Redwood-managed keys and control plane. Good for non-PHI or when you can accept vendor-managed KMS and our BAA.
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated GPU pool in our infra; logical isolation, predictable throughput. We can provide expanded audit logs and longer trace retention.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-controlled networking + option for customer-managed KMS, full control of ingress/egress — best for PHI-first workloads or strict audit controls.

Security/compliance evidence we can provide (we will attach the baseline docs):
- SOC 2 Type II report (summary + scope) — see attached redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
- BAA draft and execution path — we can push a standard BAA and iterate
- Network architecture diagram for each deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Data flows & retention policy (what we persist, KV cache considerations)
- Encryption at rest (AES-256) and TLS in transit details; KMS integrations for Private deployments
- Audit logs & retention (per-route tokenization, request traces)
- Pen test summary and third-party scan attestations

Specific items you flagged during the call:
1) PHI handling: you indicated inference inputs will contain PHI and want assurance around isolation + key ownership. For PHI we recommend Private VPC or Dedicated with a signed BAA and agreed ops SLOs.
2) SOC2 scope: you want the inference runtime and KV cache explicitly in scope — noted; we can provide an extract and map of controls.
3) Vendor questionnaire: please send your vendor security questionnaire (we can fill it) — if you send it today we aim to return it within 3 business days.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Marissa to share SOC2 + HIPAA quickstart docs (attached) — today (done).
- Alicia to send vendor questionnaire — requested by 2027-06-07.
- Schedule a 60-minute security deep dive with Rishi & Karthik w/c 2027-06-07; suggested slot: Tue 2027-06-09 10:00 PT.
- After questionnaire review, we will propose whether Dedicated pilot or Private engagement is most appropriate and provide a tentative SOW/BAA.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-hipaa-quickstart.pdf

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@medovation.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@medovation.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting eligibility synthesis + audit evidence asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from the security team’s perspective:

- KMS: for Private we need customer-managed KMS (or HSM backed) — does Redwood support CMK import / customer key control in the Private package? If not fully supported, what is the timeline and mitigation (e.g., envelope encryption)?
- Data at rest: can you confirm whether any inference artifacts (KV cache, prompt logs) are persisted in Hosted by default and whether they can be disabled / expired? We need the default retention and the option to opt-out.
- SOC2 scope: we’ll attach our questionnaire but highlight Q12 which asks whether the inference runtime and any caching layers are included in the Type II scope — please mark this explicitly.

I attached our vendor questionnaire as "vendor-security-questionnaire-2027.xlsx" — can your security team fill this and return by end of day Wednesday (2027-06-09)? Our audit window opens 2027-06-14 so we’ll need the docs in advance.

Also noting: our legal may request a bespoke BAA addendum; happy to review a draft.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Moore
Head of Security & Compliance | Medovation Health
alicia.moore@medovation.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@medovation.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting eligibility synthesis + audit evidence asks

Thanks, Alicia — looping in here with some clarifications and a short note attached (kms-integration-note.txt). TL;DR: Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem HSM-backed integrations; Dedicated can be configured to use customer KMS for key wrapping with a short ops lead time. Hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default but supports envelope encryption patterns and a BAA.

To answer your bullets: 
- KMS: Private VPC deployment can be configured with your KMS (we support AWS KMS external key policies and bring-your-own-HSM for on-prem). For Dedicated we can set up a customer key-wrap flow; this requires an ops window during provisioning (~2–3 weeks). See attached note for integration points.
- Data persistence: Hosted retains transient request logs for 7 days by default (used for debugging/abuse detection) and KV cache is persisted per-model with configurable TTLs. For PHI use we recommend disabling KV persistence or setting TTL to 0 and using Private or Dedicated with BAA. We can provide a retention matrix and a configuration guide in the deep-dive.
- SOC2 scope: Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II covers the inference runtime and the management plane; I will extract the controls mapping for KV cache and runtime and annotate the returned questionnaire.

Action items on our side:
- Fill your questionnaire and return by EOD 2027-06-09 (we’ll aim earlier).
- Provide a controls map extract for the SOC2 report covering runtime + cache — ETA 2027-06-10.
- Schedule technical deep-dive on Tue 2027-06-09 10:00 PT (Marissa, can you confirm this slot).

Karthik — can you be on the call to walk through Dedicated provisioning timeline and any infra-specific mitigations?

-Rishi
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moore <alicia.moore@medovation.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting eligibility synthesis + audit evidence asks

Alicia —

Appreciate the quick reply and the questionnaire. Confirming the next steps and the call time:

- Security deep-dive: Tue 2027-06-09 at 10:00 PT (Rishi / Karthik / Marissa) — invite sent separately.
- Questionnaire: please return vendor-security-questionnaire-2027.xlsx by EOD 2027-06-09; Rishi will annotate controls and we’ll return the completed sheet.
- Deliverables from Redwood: SOC2 controls extract (2027-06-10), draft BAA template and execution path (2027-06-11), retention matrix and deployment architecture diagrams (2027-06-11).
- Recommendation: given you’ll process PHI, we recommend Private VPC or Dedicated with customer KMS. We’ll surface the tradeoffs (time to provision, cost, monitoring) during tomorrow’s call and can scope a short Dedicated pilot if you want to test inference throughput without moving to Private.

I’ve attached the documents we discussed and included links to the Drive folder (see top of thread). If you want the BAA in DocuSign early, I can route a draft to your legal after the call.

Thanks again — looking forward to the call.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
